title: What If You Could Never Feel Pain?

scenes.text: What if you never felt pain? It sounds like a superpower. It isn't.
A rare condition called congenital insensitivity to pain does exactly this. People can still tell hot from cold, but nothing hurts.
Babies often bite their own tongues and fingers without noticing. Cuts, bruises and broken bones pile up unfelt.
Pain is the alarm that makes you rest an injury. Without it, joints wear out, and joint damage is almost universal in older patients.
Infections can go unnoticed too, and some people cannot sweat, which can cause repeated fevers.
It is extremely rare, roughly one in a million. Pain is not the problem. It is the warning system that keeps you alive.

description:
What if you could never feel pain?
It exists as a rare condition, and it is far more dangerous than it sounds: unnoticed injuries, joint damage and infections.
